--- title: "Neighbors Right, Picture Wrong" subtitle: "On a train/dev/test split, UMAP and t-SNE place held-out points beside their own kind; the arrangement of the groups they draw is arbitrary, and no held-out loss can catch it" description: "Five clustering datasets split into train, dev and test sets, with PCA, UMAP and t-SNE fitted on train only. UMAP and t-SNE keep more held-out neighbors and classify held-out points better than PCA, but PCA wins the class-centroid distance correlation on three of five sets — the metric an elephant-shaped fake also passes. Dev-set tuning buys at most 0.003 on test. Neither method has a reconstruction loss or any comparable held-out value, so no setting can be chosen and no failure can be flagged." author: "Ravi Kalia" date: "2026-11-22" categories: [Machine Learning, Statistics] image: "./cover.png" tags: [UMAP, t-SNE, PCA, clustering, train-dev-test, elephant, validation, hyperparameters] jupyter: umap-tsne-blog resources: - requirements.txt format: html: toc: true number-sections: true code-fold: true execute: warning: false --- ![Neighbors Right, Picture Wrong](./cover.png) This post splits five clustering datasets into train, dev and test sets, fits PCA, UMAP and t-SNE on the training points only, and asks which parts of the resulting picture survive on points the fit never saw. A held-out point is the simplest check a map can face: a new cell or digit should land beside its own kind. UMAP and t-SNE pass it. The part of the picture people actually read — which groups sit near which, and how far apart — is the part the check cannot see. ## The split Five datasets, all offline and deterministic: - **PBMC 3k**: 2,638 cells in 50 principal components with eight annotated types, from the 10x Genomics PBMC tutorial, cached in this repo's [When UMAP Lies series](../when-umap-lies/). Real single-cell data; a wrong grouping changes a cell-type call. - **Digits**: 1,797 8×8 handwritten digits in ten classes, scikit-learn's loader. MNIST at lower resolution, where the methods are usually shown at their best. - **Noisy clusters**: 3,000 points, five Gaussian clusters in five dimensions plus 45 noise dimensions. Stands in for real data where a small signal sits in a large feature space; a method that follows the noise has found nothing useful. - **Branched trajectory**: 3,000 points along a trunk that splits into four branches, in 20 dimensions. Stands in for a differentiation path where branch identity and the shared trunk are both real structure. - **Nested clusters**: 3,000 points, three broad groups each holding three subgroups, in 20 dimensions. Stands in for a hierarchy with genuine structure at two scales. Each set is split by stratified sampling into 60% train, 20% dev and 20% test. Scaling uses training statistics only. Every method is fitted on the training points alone; dev and test points are placed afterwards with `transform`. Three scores read the map: - **Held-out neighbor recall**: of a test point's ten nearest neighbors in the original space, the fraction that are also among its ten nearest training points on the map. - **Held-out 10-NN accuracy**: majority vote of a test point's ten nearest training points on the map, scored against its label. - **Centroid distance correlation**: Spearman correlation between pairwise distances of class centroids in the original space and in the full 2-D map. This is the distance metric that an [elephant-shaped fake passes](../when-umap-lies/). PCA also reports a squared reconstruction error on held-out points. UMAP and t-SNE report no comparable value. ::: {#fig-heldout .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} rows, table, recon, short = {}, [], {}, [] for loader in DATASETS: X, y, name = loader() Xtr, Xdev, Xte, ytr, ydev, yte = split(X, y) Xfull = np.vstack([Xtr, Xdev, Xte]) yfull = np.concatenate([ytr, ydev, yte]) scores = {} for method in ("PCA", "UMAP", "t-SNE"): Ztr, Zdev, Zte = embed(Xtr, Xdev, Xte, method) scores[method] = ( knn_acc(Ztr, ytr, Zte, yte), neighbor_recall(Xtr, Ztr, Xte, Zte), centroid_rho(Xfull, yfull, np.vstack([Ztr, Zdev, Zte])), ) p = PCA(n_components=2, random_state=0).fit(Xtr) recon[name] = float(((Xte - p.inverse_transform(p.transform(Xte))) ** 2).mean()) short.append(name) for label, idx in (("10-NN accuracy", 0), ("neighbor recall", 1), ("centroid rho", 2)): table.append({"dataset": name, "score": label, **{m: round(scores[m][idx], 3) for m in ("PCA", "UMAP", "t-SNE")}}) rows[name] = scores display(pd.DataFrame(table)) display(pd.Series(recon, name="PCA held-out reconstruction MSE").round(3).to_frame()) fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(12, 4.2)) for ax, (title, idx) in zip(axes, [("Held-out neighbor recall", 1), ("Centroid distance correlation", 2)]): x = np.arange(len(short)) for i, (m, colour) in enumerate(COLOURS.items()): ax.bar(x + (i - 1) * 0.26, [rows[n][m][idx] for n in short], 0.26, label=m, color=colour) ax.axhline(0, color="black", linewidth=0.8) ax.set_xticks(x) ax.set_xticklabels(short, rotation=30, ha="right") ax.set_title(title) ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False) fig.legend(*axes[0].get_legend_handles_labels(), loc="upper center", bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, 1.02), ncol=3, frameon=False) fig.tight_layout(rect=(0, 0, 1, 0.93)) fig.savefig("figures/heldout.png", dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight") plt.show() ``` ::: {#fig-heldout-1 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` Two of the three scores, by dataset and method. Held-out neighbor recall rewards local structure; class-centroid distance correlation rewards the global arrangement. UMAP and t-SNE win the first on every set; on the second, PCA wins three of five. ::: ::: {#fig-heldout-2 .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](index_files/figure-html/fig-heldout-output-3.png){#fig-heldout-3} ::: ::: Three results stand out: - **Local structure holds.** UMAP and t-SNE keep more of a held-out point's original neighbors on all five sets: on PBMC, t-SNE keeps 0.168 and UMAP 0.045 against PCA's 0.009; on digits, 0.507 and 0.419 against 0.133. Held-out 10-NN accuracy beats PCA on four sets for UMAP and three for t-SNE; on noisy clusters t-SNE falls to 0.917 against PCA's 0.930, and all three reach 1.000 on nested clusters. - **Global structure does not.** PCA wins centroid distance correlation on three of five sets: on PBMC it scores 0.831 against UMAP's 0.214 and t-SNE's 0.248; on nested clusters 1.000 against 0.500 and −1.000. - **The metric an elephant passes is the one they lose.** Chari and Pachter put cells on an elephant silhouette and found it matched UMAP and t-SNE on distance metrics ([Part 1](../when-umap-lies/)). Centroid correlation is that kind of metric, and UMAP and t-SNE lose it to PCA here. ## No loss to choose The routine of fitting on train, choosing on dev and confirming on test needs a score that ranks settings against a fixed target. PCA supplies one: squared reconstruction error on held-out points, 0.969 on PBMC and 1.258 on digits, computed against the same data for every number of components. UMAP and t-SNE supply none, so the nearest substitute is a held-out score of neighbor keeping. ::: {#cell-dev-choice .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} choices = [] for dataset in (load_digits, load_noisy_clusters): X, y, name = dataset() Xtr, Xdev, Xte, ytr, ydev, yte = split(X, y) Ztr_def, _, Zte_def = embed(Xtr, Xdev, Xte, "UMAP") default_umap = knn_acc(Ztr_def, ytr, Zte_def, yte) Ztr_def, _, Zte_def = embed(Xtr, Xdev, Xte, "t-SNE") default_tsne = knn_acc(Ztr_def, ytr, Zte_def, yte) for method, grid in ( ("UMAP", [(nn, md) for nn in (5, 15, 50, 100) for md in (0.0, 0.1, 0.5, 0.99)]), ("t-SNE", [(p,) for p in (5, 10, 30, 50)]), ): best = (-1, None) for setting in grid: kw = ({"n_neighbors": setting[0], "min_dist": setting[1]} if method == "UMAP" else {"perplexity": setting[0]}) Ztr, Zdev, _ = embed(Xtr, Xdev, Xte, method, **kw) acc = knn_acc(Ztr, ytr, Zdev, ydev) if acc > best[0]: best = (acc, setting) dev_acc, setting = best Ztr_winner, _, Zte_best = embed(Xtr, Xdev, Xte, method, **dict( n_neighbors=setting[0], min_dist=setting[1]) if method == "UMAP" else dict(perplexity=setting[0])) test_acc = knn_acc(Ztr_winner, ytr, Zte_best, yte) default = default_umap if method == "UMAP" else default_tsne choices.append({"dataset": name, "method": method, "dev winner": str(setting), "dev acc": round(dev_acc, 3), "test acc": round(test_acc, 3), "default test": round(default, 3), "gain": round(test_acc - default, 3)}) display(pd.DataFrame(choices)) ``` ::: {#dev-choice .cell-output .cell-output-display} ```{=html}
dataset method dev winner dev acc test acc default test gain
0 digits UMAP (5, 0.0) 0.956 0.967 0.967 0.000
1 digits t-SNE (10,) 0.956 0.972 0.978 -0.006
2 noisy clusters UMAP (50, 0.1) 0.970 0.970 0.967 0.003
3 noisy clusters t-SNE (30,) 0.937 0.917 0.917 0.000
``` ::: ::: Picking the best setting on dev buys at most 0.003 on test, and on digits the t-SNE winner scores 0.972 against the default's 0.978. The default is already as good as the search. With no held-out loss, every value of `n_neighbors`, `min_dist` and perplexity produces a valid map, and the dev score itself has a neighborhood size to set. No target stays fixed across settings, so a dev set cannot choose one, and a test set has nothing to confirm. The local win is real, but it is a win about which points sit together — not about the picture drawn around them, and not about a map you could check on new data. ## Constraints The local result is not in doubt: on these splits, UMAP and especially t-SNE place held-out points beside their own kind better than 2-D PCA. The claim here is narrower — the global arrangement those points inherit is not validated by anything in the fit. Centroid correlation over eight PBMC classes is sensitive to the two small classes, and t-SNE's out-of-sample placement is openTSNE's interpolation with its own settings, not a function learned by the fit. Five datasets and one split seed do not settle every dataset. Near. Right. Far. Wrong. Held. Out. No. Loss. No. Check. ## References - Chari, T. & Pachter, L. (2023).
